title: HTML versus XHTML: parsing and serialization rules
learningObjectives: Explain html versus xhtml: parsing and serialization rules and its role in modern HTML.
Select the correct elements, attributes, APIs, or browser behaviour for a practical use case.
Distinguish current practices from obsolete, limited, or legacy techniques.
Build and inspect a working example while considering accessibility and maintainability.
Diagnose common implementation errors and explain the trade-offs of the chosen approach.

understand.concept: HTML and XHTML can describe similar document structures but use different parsing rules. HTML served as text/html is parsed with the HTML parser, which has defined error-recovery behaviour. XHTML is HTML expressed using XML syntax and must be well-formed: elements must be properly nested and closed, attribute values quoted, and case rules followed. XHTML served as application/xhtml+xml is parsed as XML, where malformed markup can cause a fatal parse error. Do not assume that adding a slash to every HTML void element makes a document XHTML; the serialization, namespace, MIME type, and XML rules all matter.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding the distinction helps developers maintain legacy XML-served content and avoid confusing HTML's tolerant parser with XML's well-formedness requirements.
understand.analogy: HTML parsing is like a proofreader who can recover from some mistakes; XML parsing expects the document to obey a strict grammar.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy simplifies browser parsing. Real parsing rules are formal algorithms and MIME type determines which parser is used.

explain.narrative: Compare a valid HTML fragment with a well-formed XHTML-style fragment. Then identify how the response media type affects parsing and why XHTML errors can stop rendering.

questions.prompt: Which parser is used for a document served as text/html?
options: The XML parser in every browser
questions.explanation: The media type text/html selects HTML parsing.

questions.prompt: What happens when XML parsing encounters malformed nesting?
options: The XML document is not well-formed and parsing can fail
The browser always repairs it like HTML
questions.answer: The XML document is not well-formed and parsing can fail
questions.explanation: XML requires well-formed markup and does not use HTML's normal error-recovery rules.

questions.prompt: Which media type is associated with XML-served XHTML?
questions.explanation: XHTML delivered as XML uses an XML media type such as application/xhtml+xml.

questions.prompt: Are HTML void elements required to use XML-style closing slashes in text/html?
options: Yes, every HTML document is XML
questions.explanation: HTML has its own void-element syntax; XML serialization rules are separate.

questions.prompt: What determines parser behaviour most directly?
options: The document's media type and parsing context
The name of the CSS class
questions.answer: The document's media type and parsing context
questions.explanation: The browser selects parsing behaviour based on the delivered media type and context.
